scope: All Level 1 requirements, static single-user browser application at https://ranterra.pages.dev; not certification. Custom domain excluded until DNS/certificate verification.

requirements.assessment: React text/attribute encoding; imported label browser regression.
Provider URLs allow HTTPS or same-origin paths, disallow credentials/backslashes and scheme-relative URLs; query text is encoded.
JSON serialization and structured worker messages; no generated executable JS.
IndexedDB object-store keys and values; no query language interpolation.
Browser engine has no OS-command interface; native validation tools use fixed executables/argument arrays.
No accepted HTML or rich-text editor; labels are plain text.
No eval or dynamic JS source evaluation in application; WASM compilation is the explicitly permitted engine boundary.
Browser DOMParser only, no server XML parser or DTD resolver; geometry remains bounded and validated by Rust.
Versioned scenario/journal limits, RF domains and laboratory profile documented.
Rust deny_unknown_fields, finite domains and bounded collections; worker validates command identifiers.
Single-user static application has no trusted backend. Rust revalidation protects experiment integrity, not a browser-owner security boundary.
Encoded NAS/N2 state machines enforce ordering, keys, COUNT, registration and session reservations; native/independent/browser tests.
Live Pages responses enforce nosniff/CSP and correct JS/WASM MIME; untrusted imports remain local data. Chromium/Firefox hosted checks pass.
React rendering plus malicious-label browser test.
Application creates no cookies.
One-year HSTS verified on live HTML, configuration, JavaScript, WASM and 404 responses at the Pages origin. Custom domain remains outside verified scope.
No application cross-origin API or sensitive server responses. Geographic providers own their CORS policy.
No server mutation endpoint or web authentication cookies.
No sensitive cross-origin API.
No remote sensitive mutation endpoint; scenario changes stay local.
Actual deployed worker JavaScript and WASM MIME/magic verified against the CI manifest and in both hosted browsers.
No WebSocket connections.
4 MB journal / 2 MB scenario; geometry, time, commands, queues and traces bounded; computation isolated in a recoverable worker.
JSON is parsed and structurally validated independent of filename extension; only scenario/journal data accepted, no execution/upload.
Imported files are never stored in a public web directory or executed.
Browser downloads use fixed names; application cannot write arbitrary filesystem paths.

MILENAGE/NEA2/NIA2 intentionally follow 3GPP algorithms. They protect only synthetic simulation messages, not actual user secrets.
NEA2 AES-CTR with separate NIA2 AES-CMAC is the supported research protocol; no web encrypted-secret store.
SHA-256/HMAC-SHA-256 KDF and replay compatibility hashing; independent fixtures.
Pages endpoint negotiates TLS 1.3 by default, accepts TLS 1.2/1.3 and rejects TLS 1.0/1.1 with server protocol-version alerts. This is a finite version probe, not a complete TLS audit.
Pages origin redirects HTTP to HTTPS; application/provider configuration requires HTTPS or same-origin URLs. No insecure provider fallback or certificate bypass is implemented.

Public Pages certificate hostname/chain verified by Node TLS and both real hosted browsers; interactive geographic tiles loaded through normal browser certificate verification. Custom-domain certificate is pending and excluded.
All 14 CI artifact hashes verified before deploying only dist; actual /.git/config and /.svn/entries requests return 404.
No real credentials accepted; configuration explicitly public; exports exclude keys. Providers receive geographic queries only.
No authenticated website data. Synthetic NAS contexts are cleared/rebuilt; local scenario persistence is an explicit feature.
Risk-based triage/update and documented advisory exceptions recorded.
Locked npm/cargo/Go/fuzz graphs audited; paste maintenance warning and isolated Go APER exception retained visibly.
Public snapshots/recordings omit key/security-context fields; only synthetic identity/wire traces exported.
